title: What momentum says about impact
target: Connect stopping impulse to average force without claiming a complete damage forecast.
criteria: Compute momentum change during a stop.
Compare average force for different stopping times.
Name information beyond momentum needed for damage.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A 12 kg model object moving at +5 m/s comes to rest. What is its momentum change?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 3 kg object rebounds from +4 to −2 m/s. What is |Δp|?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A model impact changes momentum by −84 kg·m/s over 0.7 s. What is average force?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: For a fixed momentum change, one surface stops an object in three times the duration of another. Compare average force magnitudes.
options: One-third as large on the longer-duration surface.
cpa.guide: Force is inversely proportional to duration at fixed impulse.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Why can an impact produce a large local force while changing Earth’s speed very little?
options: Local force has no relation to impulse.
Earth receives no momentum in any collision.
Earth’s enormous mass makes its Δv = J/M tiny for the transferred impulse.
cpa.guide: Large force over a short time can transfer momentum to a very massive Earth with small Δv.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: What information beyond momentum change is needed to assess local damage?
options: Stopping time, contact area, materials, and energy transfer.
Only whether momentum is measured in SI units.
cpa.guide: Momentum alone cannot specify force distribution or material failure.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
